title: AI use fuels frustration as Hong Kong customer service complaints top 2025 total
source_used: The Standard (Hong Kong), via Google News (SCMP page blocked, 403)
key_facts: Hong Kong's Consumer Council received 3,078 customer-service complaints in the first nine months of 2026, up more than 60% year on year and above the whole of last year.

Asked if AI customer service drove the rise, council chief executive Alaina Shum Jiu-fai said AI-related complaints were 158 cases, a relatively small share; the main issue is human customer-service quality.
Vice-chairman Tony Pang Chor-fu said a rigid mandatory rule forcing AI to transfer users to a human after a failed reply would be impractical.
Common complaints: merchants not responding, being unreachable or impolite, slow follow-up.
The council's Complaint Handling ePlatform has handled more than 30,000 complaints.
quote_evidence: The Consumer Council received 3,078 customer-service complaints in the first nine months of this year, up more than 60 percent year on year and exceeding the total recorded for the whole of last year.

Asked whether the increase was driven by the growing use of AI customer service agents, Consumer Council chief executive Alaina Shum Jiu-fai said AI-related complaints accounted for 158 cases, a relatively small share of the total.
why_it_matters_hint: Complaints are rising sharply, but AI is only a small part, per the council.
event_date: Figures as of September 2026; reported 15 Oct 2026
notes: SCMP article (the pool item) was blocked; The Standard reports the same Consumer Council figures. SCMP headline links the rise to AI use; the council’s own numbers show AI is a small share. Pool score 5 lowered to 4.
